title: Sex Discrimination Amendment (Prohibiting All Sexual Harassment) Bill 2021
short_title: Sex Discrimination Amendment (Prohibiting All Sexual Harassment) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would replace setting-specific sexual harassment prohibitions with a general prohibition, extending protection and personal liability to people omitted from existing workplace categories.
It would remove the separate provisions listing covered situations and expressly reach conduct connected with Commonwealth laws, programs and functions, alongside registered organisations.
Members of parliament, judges, statutory appointees, contractors and gig workers would be protected and personally liable, with the amendments commencing on Royal Assent.
changes: The state public servant exemption from Commonwealth sexual harassment law would be repealed.
Liability for aiding or abetting unlawful conduct would extend to sexual harassment.
The Act's objects would lose words limiting sexual harassment protections to specified public settings.
summary.affected: Workers, contractors, gig workers, state public servants, parliamentarians, judges and other statutory appointees are affected.

speeches.speaker: Zali Steggall
speeches.brief: The Sex Discrimination Amendment (Prohibiting All Sexual Harassment) Bill 2021 was moved to prohibit sexual harassment in all circumstances, including for MPs and judges, citing gaps in current law highlighted by the Respect@Work report and allegations involving Dyson Heydon and Parliament House. The bill cites that one in three Australians experienced workplace sexual harassment in five years, workplace harassment costs the economy $3.5 billion annually, and only three of the Respect@Work report's 55 recommendations have been partially implemented.
